## Purpose

Track the rules decisions needed to write the Dreamrules rulebook. Each question that needs verification gets its own child issue so Norbert can send a direct link to the Dreamrules council.

This map concerns game rules and rulebook content. It does not authorize application changes or publication of an unverified rulebook.

## Agreed working process

Confirmed by Norbert on 4 October 2026:

- Ask one grilling question at a time, with the relevant evidence and a recommendation.
- Treat answers such as "I think it's this, but I need to verify" as provisional, never as confirmed rules.
- Create one GitHub issue for each uncertain question immediately after it arises. Split independent questions even when they concern the same phase or faction. Reuse an existing issue when it is the same question.
- Label these issues `question` and `wayfinder:grilling`, and link them here using native sub-issues.
- Make each issue understandable to a council member without access to the Codex conversation or local files. Include the precise question, a concrete game situation when useful, conflicting source passages with document versions and page references where available, Norbert's tentative answer, and the exact confirmation needed.
- Use public source links where available. When a source is only a local document, include the relevant short excerpt and its title/version rather than an inaccessible filesystem link.
- Mark unresolved issues "Awaiting council verification". Record the tentative answer separately from the final ruling, including who supplied it and when.
- Norbert shares the links with the council. Creating an issue does not authorize contacting council members or posting elsewhere.
- When Norbert confirms a ruling or provides council evidence, record the final answer, its source and date, and any rulebook consequences. Post the resolution, close the issue and add a linked summary under Confirmed rulings below.
- Continue independent questions while verification is pending. Pause only questions or definitive rulebook wording that depend on an unresolved ruling. A working draft may identify a provisional rule with its issue link, but must not present it as settled.
- Record confident answers directly in this map's decision log. Agreement with the research analysis does not confirm every candidate rule or settle the book's scope.

## Current state

The working [Dream Rulebook](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit) is owned by Central, uses the square 255 x 254 mm format, and has 82 draft pages at revision 29. The approved Shipment and movement chapter occupies pages 22-28, and the approved combat chapter occupies pages 29-39. Integration and Storybook cleanup are complete under #1886; supporting blocks shipped in #1887. Its substantive contents remain unpublished. The original A4 draft is preserved as a separate backup.

The main book includes Atreides, Harkonnen, Emperor, Spacing Guild, Fremen, Bene Gesserit, Bene Tleilax and Ixians. Iduali, Moritani and Ecaz are playtest factions and are excluded; separate booklets remain a future option.

Quickstart v0.8 is the starting point for current rules. A possible future revision does not make a current rule uncertain. Confirmed decisions stay settled; ask only about actual conflicts or missing details. Nineteen council-question issues remain open. #1836 is confirmed; #1843 and #1846 follow the selected v0.8 baseline.

Norbert approved the opening page explaining the design goals and high-level changes, including removal of the Guild stallout and separation of Nexus from Shai-Hulud. He also approved circled phase icons and a shaded example block; #1858 is merged and deployed. The approved phase treatment is retained in the full manuscript, with all ten icons verified live. The substantive manuscript remains unpublished.

## Research agenda

These are research areas. Each unresolved ruling has its own linked council issue:

- Book audience and faction scope.
- Nexus trigger, deck and timing.
- Spice-deck composition, prepared setup and Fremen information.
- Turn and phase sequence.
- Battle timing, including traitors, Break Conditioning, Guild retreat, Zoal and Spite.
- Supplies and Fanatical Tactics interactions.
- Bribe piles, binding deals, written notes and Truthtrance.
- Tech-token inventory, acquisition and victory contribution.
- Victory precedence, infiltration, prediction and the end of turn ten.
- Missing or outdated Karama interactions.

## Research sources

- Live Dreamrules ruleset and linked factions: https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules
- Dreamrules Quickstart Guide v0.8, supplied DOCX, last-modified metadata 7 July 2026.
- Dreamrules Quickstart Guide v0.7, PDF export 11 April 2024.
- Dreamrules Quickstart Guide v0.41, PDF export December 2022.
- Recovered JSX rulebook from the parent of commit `828a36c1e54`, under `src/game/book/dreamrules`, plus its 38-page PDF export.
- Sandbox: Dune Dreamrules Podcast, supplied planning outline. Historical questions and design intent, not adopted rules.
- Public TTS mod and dated changes: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2859509846
- Pine's unfinished Dreamrules page: https://pinecone.rodeo/bg/dreamrules.html

The production faction sheets are useful candidates for current faction rules, but production descriptions also contradict one another. The linked asset collections are incomplete. Use the user-selected v0.8 baseline for current general rules. Track genuine missing details and contradictions separately.

## Confirmed rulings

Confirmed by Norbert on 4 October 2026:

- Use Quickstart v0.8 as the current baseline.
- The normal sequence is Storm, Nexus, Spice Blow, CHOAM Charity, Bidding, Revival, Shipment and Movement, Battle, Spice Collection, Mentat.
- Turn one places the storm at a random sector, commonly determined by two players dialing their battle wheels. This detail is unchanged from GF9.
- The ten-card Nexus deck contains 1 through 7 and three blanks. Check after Storm; a number strictly below the current turn causes a Nexus. Return the card and reshuffle after every check. This replaces older worm and full-storm-rotation triggers. Full ruling and example: #1836, closed as resolved.
- Separating Nexus gives it its own probability curve. It allows the designers to tune worm frequency for spice-collection danger and Fremen mobility independently of Nexus frequency.

## Confirmed cover direction

Use the approved rainbow-sky sandworm artwork based on `dune-assets/cover/dreams-b.png`. Norbert approved the AI extension and revised rainbow arcs. The DUNE logo is a separate cover control, never baked into the image. The lower cover title reads "dream rulebook". The Dreamrules rainbow preset shipped in #1833.

Norbert owns product and rules decisions. Codex handles implementation, QA and technical reviews through agents. Show concrete work for product approval before code reviews or PRs; do not ask Norbert to conduct technical PR reviews.


## Historical manuscript progress, 4 October 2026

Central's square draft is revision 14 with 53 pages, ready for one joint product and rules pass. The user requested a broad supported drafting batch instead of page-by-page approvals.

Added setup; all phases; battle planning, timing and results; alliances and deals; tech tokens; victory; glossary; current start/free-revival values for all eight finished factions; and twelve illustrated card-reference pages inspired by the old JSX rulebook. The 36 named card entries have stable anchors. Current card art is used where available, with stock illustrations or symbols elsewhere. Final card names and copy counts remain under #1862.

The approved cover and introduction are unchanged. The substantive draft remains unpublished; Edition 1 is still the published edition.

Validation: production contents read back exactly, all 176 preview images loaded, no overflowing text regions, and a 53-page square review PDF inspected across all pages.

New council questions: #1859, #1860, #1861 and #1862. The v0.8 baseline resolves #1843 and #1846 for this draft. #1844 now asks only about exceptional-result tech awards. Nineteen questions remain open and appear in the two-page council register.

[Open the saved Central draft](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit)


## Latest manuscript progress, 6 October 2026

Completed the broad first-draft pass under #1889 directly in Central's saved book. Revision 29 contains 82 pages. Sixteen pages changed, including four new pages: Nexus, Shai-Hulud, Spice mines and Bidding. The approved combat and movement chapters remain unchanged.

Refined Storm, CHOAM Charity, Revival, Spice Collection and Mentat. Corrected the general ally-coexistence rule and Hajr reference to match Norbert's confirmed rulings. Nexus is independent of the Spice deck and Shai-Hulud. The contents page and council-question register match the current manuscript.

Used existing rulebook blocks only, with no application changes or Storybook prototypes. Schema and render validation passed, every asset reference resolved, all 82 pages were checked for overflow, and each changed page was visually inspected. Production readback matches the submitted manuscript exactly. Edition 1 remains published; the substantive draft awaits product review before publication.

Nineteen council questions remain open. Spice deck preparation and draw-pile structure are the main first-game gaps; their source conflicts remain explicit rather than being silently resolved.

Confirmed faction scope, 4 October 2026

The main Dreamrules rulebook includes finished factions only. Iduali, Moritani and Ecaz are still in playtesting and are not part of the official ruleset. Exclude all three from the main book. They may each receive a separate booklet later; that remains an option.

This is Norbert's confirmed editorial decision, not a council question.

Confirmed ownership requirement, 4 October 2026

Create the Dreamrules rulebook under Norbert's **central** account, not **P2**. Verify the active account and document ownership before creating or saving the book. This requirement comes directly from Norbert.

No Dreamrules rulebook has been created by this work yet. #1833 adds a shared cover option; it does not create a book or assign ownership.

The working draft is now created under Central: [Dream Rulebook editor](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit). It uses A4 and Illustrated classic. The substantive draft has not been published as a new edition.

These questions are unresolved source conflicts, not adopted rulings or answers supplied by Norbert. Each has its own council ticket:

- #1835: What is the current turn sequence, including turn one?
- #1836: Does the ten-card Nexus deck replace all other Nexus triggers?
- #1837: Are Spice Blows drawn from one prepared deck or two?
- #1838: What is the exact Shai-Hulud count and deck setup recipe?
- #1839: Does Guild Retreat resolve before or after Break Conditioning?
- #1840: Can Vladimir's Spite swap cards from the Supplies cache?
- #1841: What is kept, discarded and committed after each special battle result?
- #1842: What are all exceptions to retaining cards through Fanatical Tactics?
- #1843: What may spice in a bribe pile be used for before collection?
- #1844: Which standard tech tokens enter play, and when are new ones awarded?
- #1845: What does the Atreides Carryall count toward?
- #1846: Which events add the four Shield Wall markers?
- #1847: What is the ordered procedure when multiple factions qualify to win?
- #1848: How does the game end on turn ten, especially without Fremen?
- #1849: Who wins when Bene Tleilax infiltrates one or both members of a winning alliance?
- #1850: May players record public deals despite the Atreides-only notes rule?
- #1851: How does Truthtrance interact with an existing binding deal?
- #1852: Which current faction advantages can Karama stop, and at which windows?

The main book includes only the eight finished factions. Iduali, Moritani and Ecaz remain outside it.

The [Central-owned Dream Rulebook draft](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit) is saved at revision 24 with 16 pages.

It includes the approved rainbow cover, introduction, game overview, Fate and special-card references, illustrated chapters for all eight finished factions, separate Infiltration and Surveyor explanations, and the council review register. Iduali, Moritani and Ecaz have no chapters or faction references in this book.

The cover option has shipped and was verified in production. The logo and dream rulebook footer remain separate from the artwork. The content pages were checked for clipping; the longer faction entries were split across columns.

This is a first draft. The final component checklist, complete setup, turn sequence, ordinary battle procedure, victory procedure and diagrams remain unfinished. All 18 council questions are still unresolved. The substantive content has not been published as a new edition.

Full saved-data and readable-text backups are retained locally alongside the research and screenshots. Editor defect #1854 tracks the hidden title controls encountered when creating the cover; this draft's title was corrected without changing the general editor.

The Dream Rulebook draft is now square, using the 255 x 254 mm preset that matches the supplied GF9 rulebook. It remains owned by Central and uses the same [editor link](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit).

The opening now has two pages:
- Why Dreamrules? explains the goals of balance, a high skill ceiling and counterplay, with removal of the Guild stallout as a motivating example.
- What changes? introduces the major terms and changes, with only a few faction highlights.

The 17-page draft has been reflowed and the editor reports no clipped text. The original A4 draft is retained as [Dream Rulebook A4 Backup](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook-a4-backup/edit). The main square book has a new record ID, pd71pdne3ggcn8gt002y7mvqnd8fnt85, while retaining the original name and URL. Substantive content remains unpublished. Product approval of the revised opening is pending.

The [Central-owned square draft](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit) now has 56 pages at saved revision 16. The approved opening and cover are preserved. The manuscript remains a draft; the published edition has not changed.

The [Dreamrules Treachery deck](https://dune.zone/assets/deck/dreamrules-treachery-deck) is reconstructed as 33 database card designs with 45 total copies, including 30 newly created designs. Its existing cardback is preserved. The rulebook references every deck design once, with quantities totaling 45, and also references the four separate Supplies cache cards. All 37 references resolve to real card assets.

Historical JSX and card stories supplied the inventory and artwork; v0.8 supplied the current starting rules. Historical stories were not restored to Storybook. #1862 retains the inventory question for council confirmation; reconstruction alone does not establish a ruling.

PR #1867 delivers the reviewed Rulebook controls, Storybook organization, and automatic Treachery title sizing. Renderer revision 3 will recapture all 40 saved Treachery cards after deployment. The release is awaiting a retry of an unrelated homepage startup check, tracked separately in #1868.

The Central draft is now revision 17 with 58 square pages. Published edition 1 is unchanged.

This pass adds circled icons to 27 page titles, 30 related-rule references, the weapons/defenses table, and two illustrated tech-token pages. Contents-page numbers match the new page order. The approved cover, introduction and existing illustrated card chapter are unchanged.

Seven missing token assets were reconstructed from the old story artwork, using v0.8 names and triggers and the current Atreides Carryall rule. The Dreamrules Techtokens bundle now contains all seven standard tokens. Carryall is separate. All token captures are ready. No media catalogue stories were restored.

All 40 Treachery cards have been recaptured with renderer revision 3. All 45 card/token references in the draft resolve to captured images. The fully loaded 58-page browser preview has no overflowing regions, unavailable assets or broken images. An independent data review found no factual or reference defects in this pass. Existing council questions remain tracked individually.

Draft: https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit
Token bundle: https://dune.zone/assets/bundle/dreamrules-techtokens

Implemented in #1870 and merged at a58318e0fa3c13af1ddc7fab634992d17911c3cd.

Production health reports that commit. Read-only verification of the Central draft confirms revision 18, all eight shaped and shadowed tokens on page 24, matching card shadows, loaded images, and no region overflow. The draft remains 57 pages; published edition 1 is unchanged.

Independent standards and spec reviews completed. The final implementation fixes image-box clipping, standalone SVG shadow delivery under the existing CSP, and shadow allowance at column edges. Local validation passed 34 focused tests, 11 browser stories, typecheck, lint, formatting, and the publisher release gate. PR CI passed in full.

Confirmed by Norbert on 5 October 2026:

> A Truthtrance play pauses the game. No binding deals, other cards, or other game actions may occur during that pause. Play Truthtrance, ask the question, receive the answer, then resume the game.

This overrides the v0.8 Double Truthtrance paragraph. The draft chapter and its worked example have been corrected. A second Truthtrance cannot interrupt a pending question. This is a confirmed rule, not a new council question.

The separate question in #1851 concerns a binding deal that existed before Truthtrance was played; this confirmation does not settle that precedence question.

Draft chapter: https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit#CTRT/details

Delivered through #1875 at production commit 3b30d422867bdcb84b0a968fb69cbd56729b7172. [Production deployment](https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/actions/runs/37275048746) passed.

Central's [Dream Rulebook draft](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit#BPLS/details) is saved at revision 26 with 71 pages. The complete readback matches the prepared manuscript. Edition 1 remains published.

The live editor shows the whole-board opening, four-step battle pages, card discards before troop losses, the separate tie comparison page, and starred-troop illustrations. The wheel assembly has its drop shadow. All five changed pages fit their regions and their referenced images load.

![Battle-plan shadows in Central's saved production draft](https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/releases/download/proof-assets-2/production-plans-shadow.png)

Three complete combat-chapter prototypes are ready for product review on the throwaway branch [norbert/combat-chapter-prototypes](https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/tree/norbert/combat-chapter-prototypes). No prototype code is proposed for main and no manuscript revision was saved.

Storybook: Rulebook > Prototypes > Combat chapter.

- A, Compact comic: seven square pages, with each changing illustration beside its rule.
- B, Guided lesson: eight square pages, larger illustrations and a separate dialing lesson.
- C, Battle table: seven square pages, with shared table visuals and ordered instructions beneath.

Run `bun run storybook --port 6016 --no-open`. The `page` control defaults to 0 for the whole scrollable chapter; other values isolate a page for inspection.

All three use the standard heading component and existing battle-wheel renderer. Prescience and Vladimir's Spite are conditional examples within the wider faction timing, hidden plans stay hidden until reveal, Harkonnen has two cards with only the known weapon face up before reveal, killed leaders have a red cross, and card disposal precedes troop removal. The full map, tie examples, special troops and exceptional results are included.

Typecheck and focused lint pass. Browser inspection found no content overflow across all 22 square pages. The product verdict is pending. I recommend A because the changing visuals make the order and consequences easiest to follow.

Norbert approved the final combat chapter on 5 October 2026: "I'm happy with this rulebook section now."

The chosen Guided lesson now has 11 pages. The other two prototypes were removed during product iteration. It covers the purpose and order of battles, dialing, leaders, plan preparation, reveal, settlement, ties, traitors, special troops and exceptional outcomes. Special troop tokens decorate the bottom of the existing rules page.

Confirmed wording from the review:

- Prescience locks only the disclosed part of a battle plan. The rest may change until reveal; undisclosed cards and their number remain secret.
- A leader or Cheap Hero is required when available. A player without either announces this publicly prior to reveal, allowing the opponent time to react, and cannot include Treachery Cards in the plan.
- A killed leader goes to the Tanks. A leader revived with Ghola can fight again, including in another territory; Ghola must be played prior to reveal during battle.

Technical delivery is in #1883. Independent standards and specification reviews are complete, with findings fixed. The prepared Central draft has 73 pages, with the approved chapter on pages 20-30. Existing page anchors are retained; the contents-page numbers and older Ghola/glossary wording are reconciled. It has not been saved yet: that follows deployment of the required block and reference support. Edition 1 remains published.

The approved combat chapter is delivered in Central's [Dream Rulebook draft](https://dune.zone/rulesets/dreamrules/rulebooks/dream-rulebook/edit#FMTS/details). Draft revision 27 contains 73 pages; combat occupies pages 20-30. Edition 1 remains published.

#1883 is merged and deployed, with required CI and deployment checks passing. Live readback matches the prepared manuscript. Every combat reference resolves; the live editor renders the cards and five decorative troop tokens.

The integration retains public page anchors and updates the two structured links that target replaced pages. The contents-page numbers and three older Ghola/leader-commitment passages now agree with the approved chapter. Layout changes use new page identities, as required by the rulebook contract.

No council question was created for these confirmed rulings. This map stays open for the remaining rulebook work and outstanding council questions.

Open-issue sweep, 14 October 2026 (main d1ecf09): this map and #1852, #1859, #1860, #1861 and #1862 stay open.

None of the five questions has a recorded ruling. No comment from Norbert or the council since 5 October settles them, and nothing merged since then touches their content. The rulebook commits after 5 October are editor and infrastructure changes (#2149, #2183, #2185). #1862's deck reconstruction and #1852's Karama chapter are drafted, but both tickets say outright that they still need council confirmation. The map itself still tracks 19 open council questions and an unpublished manuscript.

To keep the council links clean, I didn't add sweep comments to the individual question issues.
